11 of the 47 endpoints, following a market from creation to payout; all of them are in the appendix. A token is the access JWT, as a Bearer header or an `httpOnly` cookie. A refusal is `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`; a bad token is 401 (4401 on the socket), a trader on an admin route 403. "No key" means no idempotency key and no stated promise about a repeat. A GET marked "can write" does so once: a first balance read mints the signup grant (ADR 0009), a first snapshot opens the market's book. A status with no code beside it, such as a bare `409`, is one the route declares in prose without naming a code, where more than one error with that status is reachable; none is listed, and the route's description in `/docs` says when it happens. `GET /health`, `GET /ready` and `/metrics`, on every service, are left out. A trade names a price limit, `max_cost` on a buy or `min_proceeds` on a sell, and a price past it is `409 price_beyond_limit` with nothing written; `quote_stale` is left for an older client that sends a `state_version` instead. An order names its own `limit_price`.
